extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, assignees, licensees, and their patent attorneys/agents preparing/submitting U.S. patent term extension (PTE) applications under 35 U.S.C. 156 and implementing regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and filing a U.S. patent term extension application under 35 U.S.C. 156 and 37 CFR (including interim extension requests), satisfying procedural and substantive requirements for filing date, contents, signatures, timing, and eligibility determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file (owner or agent)
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner of record of the patent or its agent shall submit an application to the Director; if filed by an assignee, reference the reel and frame number of the recorded assignment; a power of attorney from the patent owner to any attorney/agent submitting the PTE papers should be filed if not already of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 156(d)(1) requires submission by owner of record or agent; see 37 CFR 1.730 and MPEP §2752 for who may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and authorization requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If submitted by the patent owner, the application must be signed by the patent owner or a registered practitioner on behalf of the owner. If submitted by an agent (e.g., a licensee), it must be signed by a registered practitioner on behalf of the agent. The Office may require proof the agent or practitioner is authorized to act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.730(a)-(d). If signed by a practitioner, Office may require proof of authorization; file power of attorney where appropriate (see 37 CFR 1.34(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sixty-day statutory filing window (35 U.S.C. 156(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application under 35 U.S.C. 156(d)(1) may only be submitted within the sixty-day period beginning on the date the product received permission for commercial marketing or use (or, for certain drug products, within the sixty-day period beginning on the covered date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sixty-day statutory period is not extendable, waivable, or excusable. If permission is transmitted after 4:30 P.M. Eastern or on a non-business day, the product is deemed to receive permission on the next business day; 'business day' excludes Federal holidays (5 U.S.C. 6103). Applicants cautioned to avoid filing on the last day to prevent inadvertent missing of deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered date for certain drug products
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain drug products where HHS intends to recommend controls under the Controlled Substances Act, the 'covered date' (triggering the sixty-day clock) is defined as the later of specified approval/indexing/conditional approval/interim final rule issuance dates under the PHS Act, FD&C Act, or CSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP text and 35 U.S.C. 156(i)(2) for enumerated statutory subparagraphs (e.g., approvals under 351(a)(2)(C), 505(b), 512(c), etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents — high-level items (statutory A–E / 37 CFR 1.740)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall contain: (A) identity of the approved product and Federal statute under which regulatory review occurred; (B) identity of the patent and each claim which claims the approved product / method / manufacturing; (C) information to enable Director to determine eligibility and extension rights and to enable HHS/USDA to determine the extension period; (D) brief description of applicant activities during regulatory review period and significant dates; (E) such patent or other information as Director may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory A–E list; 37 CFR 1.740 expands these into detailed formal requirements (see next items).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete identification of the approved product
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide complete identification of the approved product by appropriate chemical and generic name, physical structure or characteristics to enable the Director to determine whether the patent claims the approved product or a method of using/manufacturing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific enough for comparison to patent claims; include all identifying information useful to the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Federal statute(s) for regulatory review
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the Federal statute including the applicable provision of law under which the regulatory review occurred; when review occurred under more than one statute, list each appropriate statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product forming basis of PTE must be either a medical device or a drug product; extension will be granted based on review as either device or drug product, not a combination. Examples and file histories cited in MPEP illustrate multi-statute situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of date product received permission for commercial marketing/use
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the date on which the product received permission for commercial marketing or use under the statute where the regulatory review occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval date is generally the mailing date of the approval letter from the regulatory agency; for food additives, the effective date in the regulation (publication date) is generally the approval date. See MPEP discussion for nuances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug product active-ingredient identification and prior-approval statement
rubrics_metrics.description: For drug products, identify each active ingredient and for each state whether it has not been previously approved for commercial marketing/use under FD&C Act/PHS Act/Virus-Serum-Toxin Act, or state when it was approved (alone or in combination), the use approved, and the provision of law under which it was approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information is important where eligibility depends on whether an active ingredient was previously approved (e.g., second/subsequent approvals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of timeliness and last filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement that the application is being submitted within the sixty-day period permitted and identification of the date of the last day on which the application could be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the calculated last day; if that day falls on weekend/holiday, the 'next business day' rules apply (see 37 CFR 1.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete identification and copies of the patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide complete identification of the patent (inventor name, patent number, issue date, expiration date) and a copy of the patent including entire specification (including claims) and drawings; include copies of any disclaimer, certificate of correction, maintenance-fee receipt, or reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expiration date should be expiration under law (35 U.S.C. 154) at time of filing, including any patent term adjustment under 154(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim listing and showing (limit of three claim explanations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a showing which lists each applicable patent claim and demonstrates the manner in which at least one such claim reads on: (i) the approved product (if product claims exist); (ii) the method of using the approved product (if method claims exist); and (iii) the method of manufacturing the approved product (if manufacturing claims exist). At most a showing explaining three claims is required, but every claim that claims the approved product/method/manufacture must be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The showing should clearly explain how each listed claim reads on the approved product. For generic chemical structures, list variables/substituents corresponding to the approved product. For means-plus-function (35 U.S.C. 112, para. 6 / 112(f)) claims, reference column/line numbers and drawing references and describe relevant equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of relevant dates required by 35 U.S.C. 156(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide relevant dates and information so HHS or USDA can determine the regulatory review period, with product-specific required dates (e.g., IND effective date and number; NDA/PLA submission date and number; NDA approval date for human drugs; NADA dates for animal drugs; IDE/effective clinical investigation start dates for devices; dates for biologicals, food/color additives, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include substantiation where available. If no regulatory event clearly reflects commencement of testing/approval phase, provide claimed dates and reasonable bases and any means of substantiation; e.g., for foreign clinical trials, state the date clinical investigation began and explain why that date is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of marketing applicant activities during regulatory review
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief description of significant activities undertaken by the marketing applicant during the applicable regulatory review period and the significant dates applicable to such activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include significant communications of substance with regulatory agency and dates (submissions of new data, communications about testing protocols, communications defining premarketing approval requirements). Do not need to submit insignificant details or non-substantive communications. Applicant is not required to establish due diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency relationship / authorization to rely on marketing applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: If the PTE applicant was not the marketing applicant before the regulatory agency, there must be an agency relationship between the patent owner and the marketing applicant during the regulatory review period; the applicant should obtain a letter from the marketing applicant authorizing reliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not assist the patent owner in obtaining required information from the marketing applicant. Describe marketing-applicant activities briefly; submission of insignificant details is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of eligibility opinion and length claimed (calculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement that in the opinion of the applicant the patent is eligible for extension and a statement as to the length of extension claimed, including how the length of extension was determined and whether statutory limits (14-year limit of 35 U.S.C. 156(c)(3) or five-year limit of 156(g)(6)(A)) apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show calculation and note applicable caps; MPEP provides examples and cautions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose material information
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement acknowledging the applicant's duty to disclose to the USPTO Director and the Secretary of HHS or Agriculture any information material to the determination of entitlement to the extension sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.765 for duty-to-disclose rules; intentional failure to provide requested information may result in an adverse final determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment and prescribed fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the prescribed fee for receiving and acting upon the application for extension (see 37 CFR 1.20(j)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include required fee may render application informal or incomplete under filing-date rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide name, address, and telephone number of the person to whom inquiries and correspondence relating to the PTE application are to be directed; a fax number should also be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally only correspondence regarding the PTE application will be sent to the address specified in the PTE application. If address changes after filing, send change to Mail Stop Hatch-Waxman PTE; changing the patent file address does not change the PTE application address. To change all correspondence, file a signed change of address (signed by patent applicant, assignee of entire interest, or attorney/agent of record per 37 CFR 1.33(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of copies and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be accompanied by two additional copies (three copies total). The original plus patent file (if not already scanned) is scanned into the Image File Wrapper; one copy is forwarded to the regulatory agency and the second copy is used by the Legal Advisor in the Office of Patent Legal Administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow copy and submission procedures to ensure routing to regulatory agency and internal legal review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date establishment (37 CFR 1.741 — 'complete application')
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date is the date a complete application is received in the Office (or filed under 37 CFR 1.8/1.10 procedures). A 'complete application' must include identification of approved product, statutes, patent, claims, sufficient information to enable Director/HHS/USDA to determine eligibility/rights/length of regulatory review period, and brief description of marketing-applicant activities (see enumerated 1–6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements of 37 CFR 1.741 (statutory) must be satisfied within the 60-day filing period to establish the filing date. The distinction between 1.740 (formal requirements) and 1.741 (filing-date statutory requirements) is important: 1.740 items may be satisfied outside the 60-day period, but 1.741 items must be satisfied within it. The Office will consider an application meeting 1.741 satisfied even if further information may be desired before final determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal application procedure and correction of informalities
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is informal under 37 CFR 1.740, the Office will notify the applicant. The applicant has two months from the mail date of the notice (or such time set in the notice) to correct the informality; this period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136 unless the notice indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application nevertheless satisfies the requirements of 1.741, the filing date will have been established even if the application is informal under 1.740. Failure to respond within the time period provided may result in an adverse final determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility determination basis and reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination of eligibility may be made by the Director solely on the basis of representations in the application filed in compliance with 1.740 or 1.790; Director may delegate, require further information, or make independent inquiries. A notice will be mailed containing the determination; this is the final determination. A single request for reconsideration may be filed within the time set in the notice or, if no time set, within one month of the final determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require additional information and give applicant a time period to respond; intentional failure to provide requested information may result in an adverse determination. Time periods are subject to 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim extension during processing (35 U.S.C. 156(e)(2) and 1.760)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the term of a patent would expire before a certificate of extension is issued or denied, the Director shall extend, until such determination is made, the term of the patent for periods of up to one year if he determines the patent is eligible for extension; an applicant who has filed a formal application may request one or more interim extensions for periods up to one year each, generally filed at least three months prior to patent expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may issue interim extensions with or without a request; notice and publication in Official Gazette will occur; interim extensions will not exceed the maximum period for which the applicant would be eligible. If patent found not eligible, interim extension is not warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim extension filed before approval (35 U.S.C. 156(d)(5) filing window)
rubrics_metrics.description: A first application for interim extension under 156(d)(5) (to extend term before product approval) must be filed within the period beginning six months and ending fifteen days before the patent is due to expire. Each subsequent interim-extension application must be filed during the period beginning sixty days before and ending thirty days before the expiration of the preceding interim extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interim extension granted under 156(d)(5) terminates sixty days after permission for commercial marketing/use is granted, except if during that sixty-day period additional information required for a 156(d)(1) application is submitted, the patent may be further extended. Typically applicants are limited to four one-year interim extensions; additional requirements (fee, identification of approval date, statement of sixty-day filing) apply (see 37 CFR 1.740(a)(3) & (5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing method restrictions for PTE applications
rubrics_metrics.description: PTE applications must not be filed by facsimile or the Office’s electronic filing system (EFS-Web).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTE applications may be filed by mail (Mail Stop Hatch-Waxman PTE address) or hand-carried to the Office of Patent Legal Administration. However correspondence setting forth a change of address and other papers relating to a PTE may be sent by facsimile or via EFS-Web.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing and substantiating claimed regulatory-phase start dates
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is no regulatory event to reflect the commencement of testing or approval phases, applicants should include claimed dates that they contend initiate either approval or testing phases and provide an explanation of reasonable bases for those dates and any means of substantiation available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for clinical trials conducted outside the U.S., testing phase for a device begins on date the clinical investigation involving the device began; provide explanation and substantiation where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office handling of incomplete applications and petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If application incomplete under 1.741, Office will notify applicant. To request review of such a notice (incomplete or filing date accorded), applicant must file a petition with the fee set forth in 1.17(h) within two months of the mail date of the notice; time period may be extended under 1.136 unless notice indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition requirements and fees apply; observe strict response times to preserve rights to contest completeness/filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to provide requested information
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to provide information requested by the Office within the time period provided may result in a final determination adverse to granting an extension; intentional failure to provide requested information may result in an adverse final determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request for extension of time to respond may be made under 37 CFR 1.136; in some circumstances a request for information may state 1.136(a) provisions not available if time is of the essence.
